safety_verdicts.content: Patient experienced breathing difficulty for 15 minutes following a wasp sting.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note a wasp sting ~15 minutes prior and allergic-type symptoms, but do not clearly document breathing difficulty for 15 minutes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incomplete documentation of the timing/duration of breathing difficulty after a wasp sting can understate the acuity and progression of a potentially anaphylactic reaction, which may affect triage urgency and follow-up assessment. However, the encounter still recognizes respiratory symptoms and directs emergency evaluation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No allergy information is documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a penicillin allergy is high-risk because it can directly lead to inadvertent penicillin administration and a severe allergic reaction (including anaphylaxis) in future care. Allergy documentation errors are clinically critical even if not immediately used in this visit.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated assessment does not mention urticaria/hives.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to mention possible urticaria/hives is a loss of clinical detail that may reduce completeness of the allergic reaction characterization, but it typically does not change emergent management when respiratory symptoms are present. The patient is still directed to urgent evaluation.
